scope: Predeclared event-model reference cases. All inputs are synthetic. These compare discrete sash position and specimen occupancy histories with hand calculations.
toleranceBasis: Times are integer milliseconds internally. The authored fixture uses whole seconds, so exact equality is required. Flags and identifiers must match exactly.

tests.test: Hold the sash 20 mm above the work position from 10 to 22 s.
SEALED-A is present from 2 to 19 s. Its intersection with [10, 22) is [10, 19).
SEALED-B is present from 14 to 26 s. Its intersection with [10, 22) is [14, 22).
Sum the two sample-specific intersections, counting both samples over their shared interval.
Inspect t = 9.999, 10.000, 21.999 and 22.000 s. At equal times, apply the event before reading the display.
Retain the identifiers of both specimens after their removal.
Set the 10 s sash event to the documented work position. Neither specimen overlaps a warning.
A completely closed sash is tracked as its own state.
Command 536 mm, beyond the 535 mm maximum. Reject the event before replay.
Classify 184.14, 184.15, 209.55 and 209.56 mm against the 7.25–8.25 in work band (7021355 Rev. 20 p. 1-6).

experimentalComparison: No independent cabinet sensor traces, aerosol challenge measurements or sterility data were supplied. The checks verify the software's discrete event calculation.
